notes:
Context: Coppercoat is a mid-stage fintech building a customer support + underwriting assistant that is latency-sensitive and regulated. They want Redwood Dedicated because of predictable throughput and VPC-only networking.

Key asks (shorthand):
- Guaranteed throughput for peak trading-hour traffic (approx 120 concurrent chat sessions; ~25 reqs/s sustained; spiky bursts to 80 reqs/s for short intervals).
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for 512-token context on customer-facing model (production target).
- Warm pool behavior critical: pre-warmed GPUs with model & KV cache so cold-starts don't violate SLO. They suggested warm-pool size ~= 10% of peak concurrency or minimum 3 nodes (they prefer explicit warm pool sizing controls).
- Autoscaling policy preference: proactive scale-up on forecasted traffic windows (cron + observed qps ramp) + rapid reactive scale-up when queue length > threshold. Scale-down should be conservative (idle window 15–30m) to avoid thrash.
- Queueing/backpressure: want a bounded request queue per tenant (max queue length 200 requests) with adaptive rejection/fallback to smaller quantized model or degraded features (no long tail blocking). Circuit-breaker on per-route basis.
- Reserved GPU planning: propose reserved pool for primary region (8xA100-equivalent) + burstable pool in secondary region. Ask for sizing guidance from Redwood Optimize (expected token throughput per GPU with q4/int8 profiles).
- SLA negotiation notes: they push for financial remedies beyond credits if sustained p95 latency breaches 3x in a month. Legal wants precise definition of "warm pool" availability and MTTR for model loads.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to 1yr reserved for 20% discount but wants automatic fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity exhausted (graceful degradation).

Customer quotes: "We cannot tolerate cold-starts during tranche settlement hours—those are business-critical." — Head of Platform.

Action items: Redwood to deliver POC runbook and capacity model, map warm-pool sizing options, provide sample SLA wording (MTTR, measurement windows), run baseline perf tests (p50/p95/p99) on candidate quantized model.
